destinations.name: Paris
destinations.introduction: Start with the streets. Stay for the stories. Explore Paris through original photographs, books and films, then find your own way into the city.

destinations.name: Rome
destinations.introduction: A city seen through different lives. Begin with fiction and cinema, then explore the researched place catalog. The personal photo archive has not reached Rome yet.

works.title: Il est cinq heures, Paris s’éveille
works.creator: Jacques Dutronc
works.description: The city at daybreak, as night gives way to another working day.
context: A morning portrait of Paris: the title places us at five o’clock, as the city begins to wake. This selection links to Dutronc’s 1968 television performance preserved by INA.
Listen for the movement between the sleeping city and the working city. This is an invitation to notice its rhythms, not a reconstruction of a walking route.

relationship.statement: Dutronc’s song describes Paris waking at five in the morning. INA identifies this specific performance and its broadcast date.

works.title: Sous le ciel de Paris
works.creator: Édith Piaf
works.recording: Édith Piaf’s interpretation · official artist-channel audio
works.description: A Paris chanson to return to beside the river or before a walk.
context: France Télévisions includes Sous le ciel de Paris among the songs associated with the capital. This record selects Piaf’s interpretation, available through her official artist channel.
The river photographs alongside this selection offer an editorial way into the song. They are original travel photographs, not evidence of a performance location.

relationship.statement: France Télévisions identifies Sous le ciel de Paris as part of the city’s song tradition; the linked audio identifies Piaf’s interpretation.

works.title: La Bohème
works.creator: Charles Aznavour
works.recording: Charles Aznavour’s interpretation · official lyrics video
works.description: An artist remembers youth and a changing Montmartre.
context: The song’s narrator looks back on artistic life in Montmartre. The arrondissement’s account of the Belvédère de la Bohème connects the song with the neighborhood.
Approach the remembered rooms and streets as a song’s story, rather than a literal account of Aznavour’s life. The official video credits Jacques Plante as lyricist and Aznavour as composer.

relationship.statement: The 18th arrondissement’s account connects La Bohème and its remembered artistic life to Montmartre.

works.title: J’ai deux amours
works.creator: Joséphine Baker
works.recording: Palmarès des chansons · live television performance, 18 April 1968
works.description: Baker’s Paris song, in a live performance preserved by INA.
context: This selection uses the performance broadcast in 1968, not the song’s original release. INA identifies Baker singing live against an illuminated Eiffel Tower set.

relationship.statement: France Télévisions includes J’ai deux amours in its selection of songs about Paris.

works.title: Les Champs-Élysées
works.creator: Joe Dassin
works.recording: Joe Dassin’s interpretation · official artist-channel audio
works.description: A familiar avenue becomes the setting for an encounter in song.
context: The song offers a cheerful imagined encounter on the Champs-Élysées. Follow its named setting into the city without treating the story as a record of a real meeting.

relationship.statement: France Télévisions includes Les Champs-Élysées among the capital’s signature songs; Sony identifies Dassin’s recording.

works.title: La Seine
works.creator: Vanessa Paradis & -M-
works.recording: French duet · Un monstre à Paris soundtrack, official film video
works.description: The river becomes a song in the animated film Un monstre à Paris.
context: EuropaCorp’s official video identifies Vanessa Paradis and -M- as the performers and links the recording to Un monstre à Paris.
Start with the duet, then explore the river photographs. The animated film’s Paris and the present-day archive are different views of the same city.

relationship.statement: The film distributor identifies this duet as part of Un monstre à Paris, with the Seine as its subject.

works.title: Paris sera toujours Paris
works.creator: Zaz
works.description: Zaz’s interpretation brings the Paris song tradition into her album Paris.
context: Zaz’s official video identifies this recording as the first single from her 2014 album Paris. France Télévisions places her interpretations within the city’s continuing song tradition.
The video’s production notes name Chelles as its filming location. Its Paris theme should not be mistaken for proof that every image was filmed in Paris.

relationship.statement: France Télévisions includes Zaz among the performers revisiting the Paris song tradition; her official video identifies the recording and album.

works.title: Florence sur les Champs-Élysées
works.creator: Miles Davis
works.description: Instrumental jazz connects the city to Louis Malle’s film.
context: Miles Davis’s official discography identifies the track as part of Ascenseur pour l’échafaud. Its connection to Paris comes through the film and soundtrack.
The official album notes describe the score’s Paris recording sessions in 1957 and its French release in 1958. The year shown here is the release year.

relationship.statement: The official discography describes Davis recording the score in Paris for Louis Malle’s Ascenseur pour l’échafaud.

works.title: Paris
works.creator: Elsewhere
works.description: Eight selections, from Paris chanson to jazz and film soundtracks. Explore each song at your own pace.

relationship.statement: An Elsewhere editorial selection of songs about Paris and music connected to the city through cinema. This is a selection, not a survey of its whole music scene.

works.title: An intro to jazz in Paris
works.creator: Oliver Gee
works.recording: The Earful Tower · conversation with Alex Freiman
works.description: Jazz musician and bookseller Alex Freiman talks about music in Paris, beside Shakespeare and Company.
context: The publisher describes a conversation recorded in Square René Viviani after Freiman’s live set. He and Oliver Gee discuss the Paris jazz scene and bringing live music to its streets.
This is an archival conversation from 2020. Its description supports the bookshop and recording-location connections; it is not a current guide to gigs or opening hours.

relationship.statement: The publisher identifies a Paris jazz conversation recorded beside Shakespeare and Company in Square René Viviani.

works.title: Walking through Paris with author-artist Jessie Kanelos Weiner
works.creator: Lindsey Tramuta
works.description: The illustrator and co-creator of Paris in Stride discusses walking, inspiration and making art in Paris.
context: The publisher’s notes describe a conversation about working as an artist and creating the illustrated walking book Paris in Stride.
Listen before a walk, then notice what catches your attention. This editorial suggestion does not claim the episode follows a particular route.

relationship.statement: The episode description connects Weiner’s illustration and walking book to her experience of Paris.

works.title: Carving Paris: How limestone built this city
works.creator: Oliver Gee
works.recording: The Earful Tower · conversation with Grégory Philippe
works.description: A conversation with a stonemason in his Marais atelier about limestone and Paris.
context: The publisher describes Oliver Gee meeting Grégory Philippe in his atelier in the Marais to discuss limestone.
The episode offers a starting point for noticing the materials around you. Specific building connections and workshop availability are not asserted here.

relationship.statement: The publisher identifies a conversation in a Marais atelier about the limestone used in Paris.

works.title: Giovanni’s Room
works.creator: James Baldwin
works.description: An American in Paris confronts desire and the difficulty of knowing himself.

relationship.statement: The publisher’s reading guide places the central love affair in 1950s Paris.

works.title: Cléo from 5 to 7
works.creator: Agnès Varda
works.description: A singer moves through Paris while waiting for news that could change her life.

relationship.statement: Criterion describes Cléo’s journey through Paris as she waits for medical test results.

works.title: Roman Stories
works.creator: Jhumpa Lahiri
works.description: Nine stories bring different lives into view across Rome.

relationship.statement: The publisher identifies Rome as the central city of this nine-story collection.

works.title: The Great Beauty
works.creator: Paolo Sorrentino
works.description: A writer looks beyond Rome’s parties and social rituals to reconsider his life.

relationship.statement: Criterion’s synopsis places Jep’s social life and reflections in Rome.
